1223-complementary-courses-27-credits: 3 and 3 from two pairs; MATH 245 and 254 are strongly recommended. 12–21 from the list (MATH 488 or 590). 0–3 with no Honours equivalent. 0–6 from the list or other 500-level MATH. Others with permission.
1224-degree-requirements-b-sc: Meet program and degree requirements (p. 1106); see SOUSA's guide. 60–63 credits, depending on whether MATH 222 is needed.
1226-program-description: Rigorous honours training in both fields and how they interact. 76–79 credits, depending on a COMP 202 exemption.
1227-program-prerequisites: Normally completed beforehand; otherwise add them on top of the program.
1227-required-courses-43-credits: If you know a programming language, skip COMP 202. MATH 251 or 247.
1227-complementary-courses-36-credits: 3, 3 and 3 from pairs (MATH 245 and 254 strongly recommended), 8–12 and 0–4 from two lists, 6–15 from another, and 0–9 of COMP at 300+ (not COMP 396). Not both MATH 578 and COMP 540.
1230-about-microbiology-and-immunology: Microbiology studies bacteria, viruses, single-celled eukaryotes and parasites, their roles in disease, food, spoilage and water, and basic life processes, and how to harness them for antibiotics, vaccines and industry.
Immunology studies how the body recognizes and fights foreign agents, leading to vaccines, transplants, and treatments for allergies, cancer, autoimmunity and AIDS.

Research: microbial physiology and genetics, pathogenesis, virology, cellular and molecular immunology, parasitology. Careers in pharma and biotech, hospitals, universities and government, or professional and graduate programs. New students should attend orientation and advising before the year starts.
1230-interdepartmental-honours-in-immuno: With Biochemistry and Physiology (p. 1203), an alternative to this Department's Honours. Physiology: McIntyre, Room 1136. Microbiology and Immunology: Glen Site, Bloc E, EM23248.
1230-location: Duff Medical Building, Room 511, 3775 University St., H3A 2B4.
1231-u1-required-courses-19-credits: CEGEP CHEM 212 exempts you; take electives instead.
1231-u1-u2-or-u3-complementary-courses-3: CEGEP CHEM 212 or 222: choose another complementary.
1232-program-description: A substantial background in the field and related sciences, for professional school, graduate study, or industry and research jobs.
1232-u1-required-courses-26-credits: CEGEP CHEM 212 or 222 exempts you; take electives instead. One of two more courses.
1233-program-description: The Major plus a U3 research project in a lab, after an advanced U2 lab course, for graduate study, medical research or lab jobs. Follow the Major in U1 and U2 with CGPA 3.50 by the end of U2. Graduate with C or better in required courses and a U3 GPA of 3.30.
1236-music-minors-and-courses: Open to Science students; ask a Science advisor what counts.
1236-music-minors-open-to-all-undergradu: Non-Music students can apply to several; see Schulich's site.
1236-music-courses-open-to-all-undergrad: You may take them without a minor; see Music Electives, and check credit with a Science advisor first.
1236-location: Student Affairs: Wirth Music Building, 7th floor, 527 Sherbrooke St. W.
1237-about-neurology-and-neurosurgery: No B.Sc. programs, but NEUR 310, in the Neuroscience Minor, is taught by Science. See p. 951.
1237-location: Montreal Neurological Institute and Hospital, 3801 University St., Room 140.
1238-about-neuroscience: Understanding the nervous system, from synapse molecules to behaviour, with cell biology, physiology, psychology, computer science and AI, across species. It explains how neurons connect, communicate and change, how drugs and disease affect them, and the basis of mental activity, and helps develop therapies.
1238-admission-to-the-neuroscience-major: 50 students a year. See the website, and complete prerequisites. CHEM 212 is added on top of the 65 credits if needed, as a prerequisite for CHEM 222.
1238-location: Adams Building, Room 23, 3450 University St. Advisor: Curtis Sharman.
1238-program-description: For Science students: 9 required and 15–16 complementary credits, 12–13 of them outside your home department and 6+ of those at 400–500. At most 6–7 credits shared with your primary program.
1238-complementary-courses-16-credits: 0–10 from 200–300 level and 6–15 from 400–500 level. CHEM 212 is needed for NSCI 200 and BIOL 200. One of ANAT 212, BIOC 212 or BIOL 201. BIOL 306 or PHGY 314.
1239-program-description: How the nervous system works, drawing on biology, biochemistry, computer science, math, psychology, physics and physiology.
1239-program-prerequisites: Minimum 65 credits; 50 students a year. One of MATH 139, 140 or 150; MATH 141 or 151; PHYS 101 or 131; PHYS 102 or 142; and the listed courses or equivalents.
1240-complementary-courses-42-credits: 3 credits from each of six lists, 6 from a seventh, and 3–6 from an eighth. With MATH 222's equivalent, take a 3-credit elective instead.
12–15 at 400–500: with NSCI 410, 9 from list A or B and 3 from the other; with BIOL 301 or 389, 12+ from A or B and 3 from the other.
